citations.text: The visible headword is 名. The entry calls it a semantic compound of 口 and 夕, explaining them through identifying oneself by speaking when people cannot see each other at night. It says the graph occurs in oracle-bone inscriptions, but there for place names or sacrificial names rather than the basic sense. It describes a Spring-and-Autumn bronze use as the basic sense, then gives a naming verb use on the 少虞 sword and describes later extensions from personal names to names of things, status, and reputation. Scan pixels inspected directly; the entry ends on this page. The passage’s unusual graph in the Qin-gong quotation was not used to support these claims.

citations.text: The visible headword is 夕. The entry says its ancient forms resemble the moon at moonrise; 夕 and 月 were originally one graph and later differentiated. It gives 暮夜 (dusk/night) as the graph’s original sense and cites oracle-bone uses with 夕 meaning evening. Scan pixels inspected directly; no continuation is needed for this passage.
